title: Three.js Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this Three.js course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: What two things make a Mesh?
questions.explanation: A mesh joins a shape with a material. The scene holds the mesh, and the renderer draws it from the camera's view.

questions.question: What does camera.lookAt choose?
questions.explanation: The camera is the viewpoint into a scene. Moving it changes what you see without moving the object itself.

questions.question: What does geometry describe?
questions.explanation: Geometry describes an object's shape. A sphere geometry uses small triangles to approximate a round surface.

questions.question: What changes when wireframe is true?
questions.explanation: A material tells the renderer how a shape should look. The wireframe option shows the geometry's triangle edges.

questions.question: How many axes are in this position?
questions.explanation: An object's position moves it along three scene axes: x, y and z. The default position is the origin, where all three are zero.

questions.question: What unit does this rotation use?
questions.explanation: Rotation turns an object around an axis. Three.js uses radians for these angles.

questions.question: What does a y scale of 0.5 do?
options: Adds half a pixel of margin
questions.explanation: Scale multiplies an object's size on each axis. A scale of one keeps its original size.

questions.question: What happens when this group moves?
options: Both child cubes move with it
questions.explanation: A Group can hold several objects. Moving the group moves all its children together.

questions.question: Which material in this example responds to light?
questions.explanation: Some materials respond to light. MeshStandardMaterial needs lighting so its surfaces can show shape and shading.

questions.question: Why base rotation on time?
options: To make the cube a static image
To make speed less dependent on frame rate
questions.explanation: An animation loop draws new frames. Using elapsed time makes motion less dependent on how many frames the device can draw.

questions.question: Why call updateProjectionMatrix?
options: To apply the changed camera projection settings
questions.explanation: A perspective camera needs the canvas aspect ratio. When the drawing size changes, update that ratio and its projection matrix.

questions.question: Why stop the animation loop during cleanup?
options: To save the cube to a database
To stop rendering a scene that is no longer used
questions.explanation: GPU resources need explicit cleanup when a scene is no longer used. Stop its animation and dispose of geometry, materials and renderer resources.
